learningObjectives: Explain the developmental sequence underlying developmental myelination.
Identify the principal cells, structures and signals involved in developmental myelination.
Connect developmental myelination to later cognition and behaviour.
Interpret clinical findings without treating development as deterministic.

anatomy.label: Oligodendrocyte precursor
anatomy.short: Proliferative cell capable of becoming myelinating glia
anatomy.detail: OPCs remain abundant and responsive across development.
anatomy.clinical: Their proliferation and differentiation are sensitive to injury and activity.

anatomy.label: Differentiation
anatomy.detail: Maturing cells extend processes and select axons for wrapping.
anatomy.clinical: Failure of differentiation can limit repair even when precursors are present.

anatomy.label: Internode
anatomy.detail: Each sheath forms a discrete internode around one axon segment.
anatomy.clinical: Internode geometry influences conduction velocity and timing.

anatomy.label: Node of Ranvier
anatomy.detail: Voltage-gated sodium channels cluster at nodes between sheaths.
anatomy.clinical: Disrupted nodal organisation can impair conduction without complete axon loss.

anatomy.label: White-matter tract
anatomy.detail: Increasing myelination changes diffusion, timing and network efficiency.
anatomy.clinical: White-matter measures reflect multiple tissue properties and are not direct readouts of one psychological function.

interaction.title: Developmental Myelination sequence
interaction.instruction: Select a component, then run the sequence to follow development over time.

stages.label: Recruit
stages.text: OPCs proliferate and respond to developmental signals.

stages.label: Wrap
stages.text: Processes spiral around axons to form internodes.

stages.label: Tune
stages.text: Sheaths and nodes mature to support precise conduction timing.

quizBank.question: The primary myelinating cell of the CNS is the:
Developmental myelination:
quizBank.explanation: Different pathways myelinate on different schedules, many extending into adulthood.

quizBank.question: Nodes of Ranvier are important because they:
quizBank.explanation: Nodes concentrate ion channels needed for saltatory conduction.

quizBank.question: Why can myelination affect cognition?
options: It alters timing and reliability across distributed networks
quizBank.explanation: Precise long-range timing supports coordinated cognitive processing.

quizBank.question: Which interpretation is most accurate?
options: White-matter imaging measures are biologically informative but not psychologically specific
quizBank.explanation: White-matter measures reflect several tissue properties and require cautious interpretation.
